title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 49–50 of the 'Longue Marche' notes, c. 1981). On the previous page Grothendieck had studied the 'actions of the second kind' of E_{K(s)} on the geometric fundamental group π of a curve U_{K/k}. He had done this only at places s where U has good reduction. He now turns to bad reduction. His model case is k = Q, K the function field of the modular curve for elliptic curves with one marked point (M_{1,1}), and s the cusp at infinity, which corresponds to a degenerate elliptic curve (the Tate curve).

This page localizes the problem. One passes to the henselization (not strict) of O_s, or more generally to a henselian trait S with residue field k of characteristic 0 (Q or a number field). Over the generic point η sits a hyperbolic curve U_η of type (g,ν), here (1,1). Write E_η = Gal(η̄/η) and π = π_1^geom(U_η) (profinite). There are two exact sequences:
(30) 1 → T → E_η → E_k → 1, where T is the inertia group. In residue characteristic 0 we have T ≅ Ẑ(1), and the sequence splits, e.g. via a choice of uniformizer and compatible n-th roots (Kummer theory).
(31) 1 → π → E_{U_η} → E_η → 1, the fundamental exact sequence of U_η/η.
Sequence (31) gives an outer action E_η → Out(π). Grothendieck asserts that the restriction of this outer action to T is surely nontrivial in the degenerate case. The parenthetical seems to say he expects triviality of the T-action to be equivalent to good reduction. Hence the outer action does not factor through E_k: the residue-field Galois group does not act outer-ly on π by itself.
He then starts: 'But every splitting of (30) ...'. On the next page this continues: a splitting yields an extension of E_k by π, i.e. an outer action of G_k on π. He asks whether it is 'admissible', i.e. comes from an algebraic curve over k, and doubts it. He suggests reading it through 'the infinity of the Teichmüller modular varieties', i.e. tangential base points at the boundary of M_{g,ν}. He then states a 'conjecture-à-tout-hasard': good reduction over S ⇔ the outer action of T on π is trivial.

In modern terms, this page sets up (i) the monodromy/inertia outer action attached to a degenerating hyperbolic curve, and (ii) the G_k-action on π obtained by splitting the inertia sequence. Restricted to π, this is the Galois action on the π_1 of the Tate curve, or of a maximally degenerate curve, at a tangential base point at infinity of moduli. The left-margin note (largely illegible) appears to remark that the T-action should be determined by the degeneration, plausibly a Picard–Lefschetz/Dehn-twist description, and that there lies the difficulty.
errors: No real mathematical error on this page. The claim that T acts nontrivially (outer) holds in the multiplicative-degeneration (Tate curve) case. In general, triviality of the outer T-action characterizes good reduction over S. Potential good reduction gives a nontrivial but finite-order outer inertia action, so the dichotomy must be phrased with care (the next-page conjecture is phrased correctly in terms of good reduction over S).
Minor notational drift: residue field is denoted k here, E_h / E_K elsewhere.

ideas.what: Inertia/residue exact sequence 1→T→E_η→E_k→1 for a henselian trait with characteristic-0 residue field, combined with the fundamental sequence of a hyperbolic curve over η, giving an outer inertia action on π
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois representation of a curve over a local field; monodromy/inertia action on π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (SGA1 / Grothendieck–Murre framework); systematic study by Oda, Ihara, Nakamura, Asada
ideas.where_published: Framework in SGA1 and the Esquisse; this specific discussion unpublished

ideas.what: Expectation (made explicit on the next page as a conjecture) that good reduction is equivalent to triviality of the outer inertia action on the profinite π_1
ideas.modern_name: Oda's good reduction criterion for curves (anabelian analogue of Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich / Serre–Tate); extended to affine hyperbolic curves by Tamagawa
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, stated in the Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts

ideas.what: A splitting of the inertia sequence gives an action of G_k on π for a degenerate curve; question whether it is 'admissible' (comes from a curve), to be understood via the boundary of Teichmüller/moduli spaces
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on π_1 at tangential base points at infinity of M_{g,n}; Tate-curve / maximally degenerate curve Galois representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Ihara–Nakamura (1997); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Grothendieck's Esquisse (Teichmüller tower)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and points at infinity in general terms

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames, as an open question, whether the outer G_k-action obtained from a splitting of the inertia sequence at a degenerate curve is 'admissible' (geometric). Later work (Ihara–Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki combinatorial anabelian geometry) studies these actions, but his precise admissibility question for split degenerations is posed here before that literature.
missed.quote: Mais tout scindage de (30), [définit une extension de E_k par π ... est-elle 'admissible' ?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck anticipated the program of studying Galois actions via degenerations / tangential base points and the 'geometricity' question for such actions.

missed.claim: The good-reduction ⇔ trivial outer inertia action statement (set up on this page, stated on the next as a conjecture) is an early, uncredited formulation of what became Oda's criterion (proved c. 1990–95).
missed.quote: Ici l'action extérieure de T sur π n'est sûrement pas triviale (je suppose que c'est l'é[quivalent] de 'bonne réduction')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: the Oda–Tamagawa good reduction criterion is normally not traced to Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up, in 1981, both Oda's good-reduction criterion (made explicit as a conjecture on the following page) and the study of Galois actions at degenerations / boundary of moduli. These are now standard results credited to Oda, Tamagawa, Ihara and Nakamura. That is a notable priority detail, but the page itself is mostly setup, and the boundary-of-Teichmüller theme is partly in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Sequence (30) should read 1 → T → E_η → E_k → 1 (residue-field Galois group), consistent with 'E_k n'opère pas lui-même extérieurement'.
'je suppose que c'est l'art des "Π_y bonne réduction"' is a misreading; plausibly '(je suppose que c'est l'équivalent de "bonne réduction")' or similar. There is no Π_y.
'un extension finie' should be 'une extension finie'.
The left-margin note is mostly illegible. It seems to begin 'mais l'action de T sur π n'est-elle déterminée par ...' and to mention 'la difficulté'; the reading 'diminuée par VA' is doubtful.
